clue.text: What Elgar did to be calm

definitions.meaning: the composer Edward Elgar wrote music, so this describes his past activity of writing scores
an adjective for someone unruffled and self-possessed

explanation.surface: A remark that the composer Elgar's achievement was serenity of mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' is only a link between the two definitions; Elgar was an English composer, best known for the Enigma Variations.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing music is the work of a composer, and a person who is collected and unflustered is described with the same word.

clue.text: Deprived child — no harp to play

indicators.note: playing with something mixes it up, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A poor child without a harp to play.
explanation.definitionFit: A child who has lost both parents is deprived of them.

clue.text: Edible seeds that may be taken when someone's ill

definitions.meaning: peas, beans and lentils, the dried seeds of legumes

definitions.text: that may be taken when someone's ill
definitions.meaning: a doctor takes a patient's heartbeat reading at the wrist

explanation.surface: Seeds you can eat that are given to a sick person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken' suggests swallowing food or medicine; the second sense is a doctor measuring a heartbeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Lentils and beans are legumes, and the throb of blood in the wrist is measured by a doctor when someone is ill.

clue.text: Fast vehicle to exhibit mark after accident

parts.note: to sport something is to wear or show it off
a scar is the mark left by an injury

explanation.surface: A speedy car showing damage after a crash.
explanation.definitionFit: A low, fast two-seater automobile is a fast vehicle, an example of the class.

clue.text: New code with drink to establish decency

indicators.note: something made new is reshaped, so the letters of code are rearranged

parts.note: rum is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: A fresh rule about alcohol introduced to keep people behaving properly.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper, seemly behaviour is decency, a synonym.

clue.text: Trendy little Maureen, attractive person

parts.note: Mo is the usual short form of the name Maureen
a dish is slang for a good-looking person

explanation.surface: A fashionable young woman called Maureen who is also very good-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean in the current fashion, a close synonym.

clue.text: Othello's desolate areas

definitions.meaning: Shakespeare's Othello is a Moor, so 'Othello is' gives the noun with 's
open uncultivated upland covered with heather

explanation.surface: The bleak wild places associated with Shakespeare's Othello.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Othello's' as 'Othello is': he is the Moor of Venice. The second sense is open heathland, as in the Yorkshire hills.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's general is a North African Moor, and bleak open heath is called moorland.

clue.text: Characters meeting in a compound

parts.note: sounds like people gathering in an enclosure, but means two vowel letters joined into one sound or ligature

explanation.surface: People getting together inside a walled enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' are letters, not people, and 'compound' is a combined sound, not a fenced area.
explanation.definitionFit: Two vowel sounds glide together in one syllable, sometimes written as joined letters such as ae.

clue.text: It isn't the euro which is excellent!

definitions.meaning: the British pound, a currency the UK kept instead of joining the euro

explanation.surface: A patriotic boast that the pound beats the European currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'which is' links the two senses. Britain kept its own currency, the pound, rather than adopting the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: The British currency is the pound, and the same word means first-rate or of fine quality.

clue.text: Divine being with head beset by a halo

indicators.note: to be beset by things is to be surrounded by them, so the word for head goes between the other pieces

parts.note: a halo is a ring, the shape of the letter O
poll is an old word for the head, still used in 'poll tax'

explanation.surface: A god pictured with a halo shining round his head.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek god of the sun, music and poetry is a deity, a divine being.

clue.text: He rakes in the money…

parts.note: reads like a wealthy man earning a fortune, but describes a casino worker who literally gathers chips across the table with a rake

explanation.surface: A man described as making a great deal of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rakes in' suggests getting rich; in a casino the table attendant uses a small rake to collect the stakes for the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino table attendant collects and pays out stakes, drawing chips in with a long-handled rake.

clue.text: …for him, smashing gas meter

indicators.note: breaking something to pieces suggests the letters of these words are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: the casino worker collects money from someone who wrecks a gas meter.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to the clue before: the croupier rakes in money for the house from a gambler, so 'for him' points to the player.
explanation.definitionFit: The croupier's takings come from a gambler, a habitual player of games of chance.

clue.text: Decide on a wooden bench

definitions.meaning: to determine or resolve a matter
a high-backed wooden seat with arms, often with a chest under the seat

explanation.surface: Someone choosing to sit on a bench made of wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on a' is a link here, though it reads as part of the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: To resolve a dispute is to fix it finally, and the same word names an old high-backed wooden seat for several people.

clue.text: Evidence of mathematician making his mark?

definitions.text: Evidence of mathematician making his mark?

parts.words: Evidence of mathematician making his mark?
parts.note: reads like proof of an academic's success, but means the small dot a number-writer puts between whole and fractional parts

explanation.surface: Asking what shows that a mathematician has become famous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making his mark' sounds like achieving fame; literally it is the dot written in a number such as 3.14.
explanation.definitionFit: The dot separating units from tenths is the literal mark a mathematician writes in a number.

clue.text: Hopeless rep, teased unfairly

indicators.note: treated unfairly suggests these letters are mishandled and rearranged

explanation.surface: A salesman, mocked cruelly, feels his position is hopeless.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a state of despair is the same as being without hope.

clue.text: Look to get round ice on street in city

indicators.note: getting round something means encircling it, so these letters go inside the word for look

parts.note: to leer is to look at someone in a sly or suggestive way
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone glancing about on an icy road in a town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link: in a down clue ICE sits on top of ST.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in the English East Midlands, an example of the class.

clue.text: Study island material

parts.note: to con is an old word for learning or studying
Crete is the largest Greek island

explanation.surface: Researching the substances found on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: The building mix of cement, sand and gravel is a construction material.

clue.text: Forcing prisoners to take exercise

parts.note: cons is short for convicts
training is working out or exercising

explanation.surface: Making inmates do physical exercise against their will.
explanation.definitionFit: Compelling someone and restricting them by force are close synonyms.

clue.text: Passionate during wild teens

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in the night'

indicators.note: running wild suggests the letters of teens are disordered

explanation.surface: Adolescents running riot and feeling things deeply.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong feeling and fervour describe both words, synonyms.

clue.text: Mistakes made by scoundrel in a particular period

indicators.note: one piece placed in another goes inside it

parts.note: an era is a distinct period of time
a rat is a contemptible person

explanation.surface: Errors committed by a villain in a certain age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made by' is a link; 'in' puts RAT inside ERA.
explanation.definitionFit: A list of printing errors is a list of mistakes, the Latin plural of erratum.

clue.text: Stress when bit of money is added to the bill

indicators.note: one piece being added to another places it after the first one

parts.note: AC is an abbreviation of account, which can mean a bill
a cent is a small coin

explanation.surface: Anxiety felt when a small extra charge appears on a restaurant bill.
explanation.walkthrough: The coin comes first in the clue but is added on, so it goes after the account.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphasis placed on a syllable or word is called by either name.

clue.text: Dickensian character in a spin

definitions.meaning: Oliver, the workhouse orphan in a Charles Dickens novel

explanation.surface: A figure from a Dickens novel who is in a whirl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a' is a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver of the Dickens novel has this surname, and the word also means a turn or rotation.

clue.text: Bank rate changed — excessive interest-taking denied us

indicators.note: altering the word rate signals that its letters are rearranged
being denied something means going without it, so letters are taken away

parts.note: usury is lending money at exorbitant interest
the clue prints us, but only a single U may be removed

explanation.surface: A complaint that a bank's interest rate rise is extortionate lending that cheats us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' gives TREA from RATE. Taking US from USURY leaves URY, too short; the answer needs SURY, so only one U goes: a slip by the setter.
explanation.definitionFit: A national finance department or a store of funds is a bank in the broad sense of a place holding money.

clue.text: Ship filled with liquid goes under

indicators.note: something filled with another has it inside, so these letters go between

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
ink is a writing liquid

explanation.surface: A vessel taking on water and going down.
explanation.definitionFit: To sink is to go down below the surface, as a ship goes under.

clue.text: Denial, say, within the country

indicators.note: one thing sitting within another means it is placed inside it

parts.note: a nation is a country
eg (for example) is what 'say' means when introducing an instance

explanation.surface: A nation-wide refusal to accept something.
explanation.definitionFit: Contradicting or saying no to something is a refusal, the same as a denial.

clue.text: Helmet that protects one knight

indicators.note: something that protects another surrounds it, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one is I
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A helmet guarding a single knight in armour.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier's metal helmet is informally called by this name.

clue.text: Have a change of mind about period of fasting

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Lent is the Christian season of fasting before Easter

explanation.surface: Someone reconsidering whether to keep up their Lenten fast.
explanation.definitionFit: To soften and give way after refusing is to change one's mind, a synonym.

clue.text: Description of ancient civilisation conjuring up centaurs

indicators.note: summoning by magic suggests the letters of the word centaurs are reworked into something new

explanation.surface: An account of an old culture that summons mythical horse-men.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the people of Etruria, a pre-Roman civilisation of central Italy.
